claims.claim_vi: Base64 of '4111 1111 1111 1111' decodes back without any key.

claims.claim_vi: A Fernet token of the same data starts with 'gAAAAAB', decrypts with the right key and raises InvalidToken with a wrong key.

claims.claim_vi: A random token ('tok_' plus random hex) mapped through a dictionary 'vault' returns the data; the token is not derived from it.

claims.claim_vi: Symmetric encryption should use AES with a key of at least 128 bits (ideally 256); dedicated secret or key management systems add protection at the cost of complexity and administrative overhead.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of the OWASP repository.

claims.claim_vi: Passwords should be hashed with modern adaptive algorithms rather than encrypted; hashing is a one-way function.

claims.claim_vi: Tokenization is often used for payment card data and helps with PCI DSS compliance.
claims.verified_by: Carried from the source as general description; not independently checked. The OWASP Cryptographic Storage cheat sheet does not mention tokenization.

design_notes_vi: Một dữ liệu mẫu cho cả ba cách để so sánh; thẻ cuối nói mỗi cách có một chỗ phải bảo vệ. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source calls tokenization 'highly secure' because tokens cannot be reverse-engineered; true for random vault-based tokens, but the risk moves to the token vault, which the lesson names as the place to protect.
Source does not distinguish hashing; the lesson adds a short note that hashing is a separate one-way operation.
